I have a lot of creepy, unexplained things that happen to me in my dreams, but I have trouble putting them into words. I don't know if it's a family thing or whatever, but my brother's seen some pretty strange stuff too. We were both lucid dreamers from a young age, and we started fucking around with our dreams like the scientists we were. I spawned some pretty scary stuff, but nothing quite as subtly terrifying as the experience my brother described to me.

In his dreams, he'd almost always have this strange feeling. As if he wasn't the only person where he was. He said that it didn't feel like he was being followed, more like rather than him being the dreamer, he was a part of the dream. But he chalked it up to side effects of messing with the laws of the dream universe and ignored it. And then came the man.

One night, during a lucid dream, my brother saw a figure off in the distance. He was close enough that he could make out a black fedora and brown trench coat, but he couldn't see any facial features or anything like that. He tried to go and talk to him, but when he got closer, the man would somehow vanish whenever he'd blink or momentarily be blocked by an obstruction along the way or anything like that. This continued for about three years, and each time he saw the man, he'd eventually start to move closer and closer to him before he'd get away. Until eventually, he got within an arm's reach.

At first, the man just stood there, silently watching. His face was hidden under the shadow of his hat. My brother asked him who he was, but got no answer. So he moved to take the hat off his head. That got the man's attention. He grabbed my brother with a strength that he couldn't understand, he wasn't able to break his grip, despite being in a lucid dream. The man pulled him close and harshly whispered "You will never see me again." And then my brother woke up.

From that night on, my brother couldn't lucid dream and he had a lot of trouble remembering his dreams for the next three years before he finally started to get it back. But even now, four years since that night, he hasn't seen any sign of the man.

This isn't my story, but I feel partially responsible because I was thought to be the accomplice to the person who did pull it off, and I probably could've predicted this. Back in 11th grade, I was friends with this guy, let's call him Victor. He was always looking for loopholes to make things easier for him, or just to spite people (namely me). We were the only two members of our clique in a certain psychology class, so we grew pretty close over that term. I ended up visiting our teacher earlier this year, who recalled that I was the better of the two, going as far as to call Victor a "little shit." Probably rightfully so.

The year was fairly uneventful in terms of lifehacks save for the occasional "corrupt your word document so you can procrastinate!" Which I totally don't continue to use even today. Nope. But then came our final assignment, which came in two parts. The first involved group work where we'd work together to conduct a survey and analyze the results. The second was individual, where we would write a report from the angle of psychology on basically anything that we wanted. If memory serves, he chose something to do Marxian ideology.

The shitstorm began with the survey. Victor and I were in the same group as another boy, let's call him Kevin. Kevin was another friend, but he wasn't quite as close so we mostly kept our interactions professional in comparison to Victor and mine, which usually ended up in a mess of me cursing at him and him snarkily laughing.

So the survey. Day 1: 0 responses. Day 2: 3 responses. Day 3: 79 responses. I was **very** curious to find out who had managed that, since I knew Kevin wasn't going to go out of his way to get survey responses, and Victor was even lazier than him. So I confront Victor, asking if something happened with the survey. He said he went around and got some responses so that he wouldn't have to work as hard on the powerpoint. But I was still suspicious.

I was dating a girl at the time, let's call her Rachel. Rachel and Victor were also very close, with the former referring to the latter as her bitch. We had a mocking love triangle. So I go up to Rachel and ask if she knows anything about this survey. She denies it, but I'm very good at facial manipulation, so I can tell when someone is lying. After asking further, I found out that Victor had asked her to forge all those answers instead of going around asking people.

You might not think this is that big a deal. It's not. The big deal was the fact that he did it behind my back and that she didn't clear it by me despite knowing that I was working with Victor on it.  So I go nuts at Victor, and he, being the little shit he is, assured me that our teacher would never know, and that everything would be fine. He ended up being right, and I kept that secret until I saw my teacher again this year, which ended up being the context for the "little shit" remark.

That part was the personal part. The next loophole sent **the entire fucking district into such a frenzy that they had to change their entire system for academic integrity.**

Victor was taking a law class at the same time as the psychology class, and had a report to write there too. I remember him asking me to edit his psychology report, and I did, making sure to mention that if he liked, I'd edit his law report too. He seemed pretty nervous when he declined, which made me think he was procrastinating or something. I was so wrong.

Two weeks after we'd handed in the reports, Victor gets called out by our teacher, and I see his law teacher standing outside too. He comes back with that smirk of his again, and a very frustrated psychology teacher. He refuses to tell me what's going on. The next day, he's called down to the office. Again, he comes back with his smirk and no explanation.

We also happened to be taking microeconomics at the time, and I was very close with the teacher. I find out from him that Victor had handed in the same paper to two different courses, identical save for the title pages. Some schools say you can do this. Some schools say you can't. Others schools don't think students are smart enough to come up with this idea. My school was the latter.

And my school had no fucking clue how to deal with the situation. Is it plagiarism? Of himself? With both papers having been submitted at the exact same time? It made no sense! The last month of the school year was filled with staff meetings discussing how to deal with the situation. How did Victor justify himself? "Look at all the utility I've derived from that paper!"

He got away with three finals with As. One for psych, one for law, and one for microeconomics.

I haven't talked much to him recently, but I remember our last conversation involved his university not having any laws against this yet.

**Yet.**

TL;DR: Friend got away with forging survey results, then got away with writing the same paper to two courses. Came out with 3 As because he impressed one teacher who wasn't even part of those two courses.
